column1: # The backtest evaluation set: the repositories this reading is measured on, as opposed to the one it was
# developed against. One row per member, and the answer for each comes from outside this project.
# Columns: name, origin, sha, licence, area, stated-by, arm
#   name        the directory the clone is expected under -Dcs.evaluation.dir
#   origin      the URL it is cloned from
#   sha         the commit it is pinned to. A reading of a moving target is not reproducible, and
#               every figure this library publishes is a reading of a named commit.
#   licence     The SPDX identifier, verified at the revision named above and not at HEAD. A member is
#               read, never redistributed, so a copyleft licence is recorded rather than refused — jPOS
#               is AGPL-3.0. Where the publisher states a licence SPDX has no identifier for, the file
#               name is recorded instead: QuickFIX/J publishes "The QuickFIX Software License, Version
#               1.0", which is BSD-4-clause-shaped and not copyleft.
#   area        the subject area the reading is expected to place the member under, named exactly as
#               the scheme states it — a field such as Computer Science, or a subfield such as
#               Finance. It is an identifier in somebody else's hierarchy, so it cannot collide with
#               another sense of a word. What it replaced could: marking a topic by whether its prose
#               said "security" marked Food Security, Pesticide Exposure and Retirement and
#               Disability, and marking by "content" marked Peanut Plant Research, where the word
#               means concentration. Worse, it marked against the reading — Tika's nearest topic is
#               Natural Language Processing Techniques, which says no "content" and was scored wrong.
#   stated-by   what the area was judged from — the repository's own README one-liner, its GitHub
#               topics or its package description. The judgement is THIS PROJECT'S and the safeguard
#               is that it is recorded BEFORE the reading is run and never revised afterwards. An
#               answer chosen after reading the tree is the same defect as choosing OLiA after
#               reading this one.
#   arm         in-domain | out-of-domain | no-taxonomy | degenerate
# Source: THIS PROJECT. That has to be said outright. Every other file bundled here is a curated
#   statement of a published standard, which is citable; this is a curated observation of a corpus,
#   which the doctrine refuses as evidence. IT IS A TEST FIXTURE AND IT NEVER VOTES. It is not on
#   the published classpath and nothing in the library reads it — only the evaluation set diagnostic does.
# Licence: this file is part of this project and carries its licence. The repositories it names
#   carry their own, which is what the licence column is for.
# What a member costs to add is: verify the licence at the revision, record the stated domain and
# who stated it, pin the SHA, and put it in an arm. Every domain needs at least one out-of-domain
# member, because a vocabulary that fires in its domain proves nothing until it is shown not to
# fire outside it, and the honest first result for those is silence.
# The domain column below is cited, not chosen: it is the category token the Apache Software
#   Foundation states for the project in its own DOAP record, published separately from the code
#   and written by the project rather than by anyone here. Cited rather than copied — one token
#   per member is a fact about that project, where a wholesale copy of the category list would be
#   an adaptation of a curated work.
# Retrieved: 2026-08-15 from https://projects.apache.org/json/foundation/projects.json
#   sha256 96fc9d38453d3ffe96b0875104c2d579ecc813fa500ec296c5a43ffece61a120, so a later run can
#   tell whether it is reading the same statement. It has since moved, which is what that hash is for:
#   the `maven` and `santuario` tokens below were read on 2026-08-19 from the same URL at sha256
#   183a631e9e926ceb955994db8672be0f49cf68401ebdfd0ca9086d7714182655, still 375 projects. A token is
#   never revised after a member is read, so the two retrievals stand side by side rather than one
#   replacing the other. That aggregate holds 375 projects, 269 of them
#   stating Java, across 644 category slots of which 115 are `retired` or `no-tlp-doap`.
# Origins are the github.com/apache mirrors rather than the gitbox or svn URLs the DOAP records
#   name, because those are what can be cloned without credentials.
# The arm is relative to the taxonomies this repository bundles. An Apache project about content
#   extraction or big data is one neither OLiA nor FIBO should say anything about, and that silence is
#   the control the industry-vocabulary reading has been blocked on. `santuario` is the exception and
#   is marked in-domain for one taxonomy only: the bundled NIST Cybersecurity Framework partitions what
#   a security project does, and until this member there was no repository to fire it on. It is
#   out-of-domain for OLiA and FIBO like every other member.
tika
